### Diagnosis

The current bug report describes an inconsistency in null handling when comparing values using the unequals operator (!=). The reported scenario involves a `Map` with values of type `Integer`, where one value is `null`.

Looking at the failing test `testMapValueEquality()` in `org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.JXPath151Test`, it seems to involve JXPath expressions and checking for inequality between values in the map using the unequals operator.

In JXPath, the expressions are evaluated using `JXPathContext`. The `JXPathContext` class is responsible for managing the context of the JXPath evaluation. The `JXPathContext` constructor takes a parent context and a context bean.

The `JXPathContext` implementation class `JXPathContextReferenceImpl` also has a constructor that takes a parent context and a context bean.

The issue might be related to how the JXPath handles null values and the comparison operation in the expressions. There could be a discrepancy in how null values are processed or compared with other values in the expressions, leading to the observed inconsistency in null handling.

### Hypothesis
The `JXPathContext` implementation might not handle null values appropriately in expressions involving inequality comparisons, leading to the reported inconsistency.

I should investigate the handling of null values in the JXPathContext and related classes to pinpoint the exact cause of the null handling inconsistency.

Next, I will provide the methods that need to be fixed based on this diagnosis.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
